reference: GNU sed from the runner's read-only /usr tree is the parity oracle; each parity case runs the same script under reference Bash with GNU sed on PATH and under bash-os with PATH empty. Cases that need multibyte behaviour export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 themselves.
coverage: UTF-8 y/// character pairing and \U \L \u \l case conversion of non-ASCII letters (guest pass 3).
a/i/c text to the end of the line in every form (one-liner, a\ plus newline, -e continuation, -f files), and sed -i through search-only directories (guest pass 6).
exclusions: Unibyte-locale y/// and case conversion are covered by suites/sed.json.

cases.purpose: In a UTF-8 locale y/// pairs characters, not bytes (y/éà/ea/ used to fail with 'SET1 and SET2 must be same length'), and \U \L \u \l convert non-ASCII letters (guest pass 3, G49).
cases.script:
export LC_ALL=C.UTF-8
printf 'éàx\n' | sed 'y/éà/ea/'
printf 'abc\n' | sed 'y/abc/αβγ/'
printf 'αβγ abc\n' | sed 'y/αβγ/abc/'
printf 'école ÉCOLE ça\n' | sed 's/.*/\U&/'
printf 'École ÉCOLE\n' | sed 's/.*/\L&/'
printf 'école\n' | sed 's/.*/\u&/'
printf 'École\n' | sed 's/\(.\)\(.*\)/\l\1\U\2/'
printf 'x\n' | sed 's/x/\Uéà\E-é/'
printf 'é\n' | sed 'y/é/ab/' 2>/dev/null || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: sed -i needs only search permission on the directories above the file and search plus write permission on its own directory, like a 0711 home directory seen by another user; it used to open every path component for reading and fail with 'Permission denied' (guest pass 6, G102). The [ -r ] lines prove read permission is really withheld.
cases.script:
mkdir -p x/w y/v
echo a > x/w/f
echo a > y/v/f
chmod 0311 x y/v
[ -r x ] || echo x-unreadable
[ -r y/v ] || echo v-unreadable
sed -i s/a/b/ "$PWD/x/w/f"
sed -i s/b/c/ x/w/f
sed -i.bak s/c/d/ x/w/f
sed -i s/a/b/ y/v/f
(cd y/v && sed -i.orig s/b/c/ f)
cat x/w/f x/w/f.bak y/v/f
chmod 0755 x y/v
ls x/w y/v

cases.purpose: Unknown commands (`k'), extra characters, missing commands, a stray `,', line address 0, multiple `!'s, a label-less `:', missing r/R/w/W filenames, unterminated address regexes and the version check report GNU's wording and character count, a newline included (guest pass 7, G105).

Braces and labels: "unexpected `}'", "unmatched `{'" at char 0, "`}' doesn't want any addresses", extra characters after `}', and "can't find label for jump to `foo'" with status 4 (guest pass 7, G105).

Regex compile errors carry the regex library's message ("Unmatched ( or \\(") and the count GNU shows, which runs to the end of the command's flags; an out-of-range \\N reads "invalid reference \\1 on `s' command's RHS" (guest pass 7, G105).

Each -e (and the program operand) is its own "-e expression #N", counted from 1 with characters counted from its start; a -f FILE error reads "file FILE line N:", "-f -" reads the script from standard input ("file - line 1:"), and an unmatched `{' in a file names the brace's line. When -e or -f appears anywhere, the first operand is an input file (guest pass 7, G105).
cases.script:
t() { local rc=0; echo x | sed "$@" 2>&1 || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"; }
t -e p -e k
t -e p -e s/a
t -e 'p;p' -e 'y/a/bc/'
t -e '1{' -e p
t -n -e p -e '}'
t --expression=p --expression=k
t -ne p -e k
printf 'p\nk\n' > f1.sed; t -f f1.sed
printf 'p\ns/a\n' > f2.sed; t -f f2.sed
printf 'p\n1{\n' > f4.sed; t -f f4.sed
t -e p -f f1.sed
t -f f1.sed -e k
printf 's/a/b/\n' > ok.sed; t -f ok.sed -e k
t -e p -f ok.sed -e k
printf 'y/a/bc/' > f5.sed; t -f f5.sed
printf 'p\n\nk' > f6.sed; t -f f6.sed
printf '1{\n' > ob.sed; t -f ob.sed -e p
printf 'p\n}\n' > cb.sed; t -f cb.sed
t --file=f1.sed
printf 'p\n' > ok2.sed; t -f ok2.sed -e 'b nolab'
t -f nosuch
rc=0; printf 'k\n' | sed -f - 2>&1 || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"
rc=0; printf 's/a/b/\n' | sed -f - in1 2>&1 || rc=$?; echo "rc=$rc"
